stories.headline: Wall Street Futures Rebound After AI-Led Correction
stories.dek: The S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory Friday, and futures pointed sharply higher Monday.
pole_a_bullets: The selloff was panic, not a broken AI thesis. Nvidia reported strong earnings and Anthropic's IPO drew heavy demand.
Part of the slide was mechanical. Funds sold other stocks to raise cash for IPO orders, and more than half of about 1,200 institutions got no shares.
A rebound does not require every problem to be solved. Investors can separate temporary valuation pressure from lasting profit damage.
Monday's futures jump shows buyers are ready to return to AI-linked shares.
pole_b_bullets: AI valuations and spending are the core issue. The Anthropic IPO highlighted bubble fears rather than easing them.
Funding is shifting. A Bank of America survey found 52% of fund managers expect a major cloud company to cut AI spending within six months.
The Fed is expected to raise rates in December. Some investors fear tightening into a slowdown if earnings and AI investment have peaked.
The Nvidia leadership and chip-export scandal and the Democratic midterm win were a one-two punch for the AI story.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by strategists such as Dan Ives of Wedbush-style bulls and Saxo's Charu Chanana, as quoted by Reuters and BeInCrypto.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Renaissance Capital, Treasury Partners and fund-manager survey respondents, as quoted by CNBC, NBC News and BeInCrypto.
evidence_left: On Friday Nov. 20 the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% to 22,617.73, and the Dow fell 1.9% to 48,147.33 (Investing.com).
The S&P 500 lost 8.6% for the week. ABC Australia called it the worst week in more than six years. Schwab and Seoul Economic Daily called it the worst since April 2025.
evidence_right: The Cboe VIX closed at 35.89 Friday, its highest since April 2025 (Investing.com).

Monday premarket, CNBC reported Dow futures up 1.97% and S&P 500 futures up 2.76%. Reuters at 2:29 a.m. ET had S&P E-minis up 2.24%. CME FedWatch odds of a December quarter-point hike were about 92% (CNBC) versus 98% (Saxo).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNBC, Investing.com (Reuters), NBC News, BeInCrypto, November 23, 2026.

stories.headline: Trump Orders Federal Contractors to Route Congressional Requests Through White House
stories.dek: The Nov. 20 executive order comes weeks before Democrats take control of both chambers.
pole_a_bullets: Executive privilege is a real constitutional protection. The White House says the order guards it from congressional overreach.
Congress needs a valid legislative purpose to seek executive-branch information. The order says requests that intrude on core executive functions fall outside that.
Contractors handle sensitive national and homeland security material. Coordinating responses prevents its release to unauthorized parties.
The White House says some lawmakers have harassed private companies that contract with the government. The order sets one process for responding.
pole_b_bullets: Oversight is a core congressional power. Rep. Robert Garcia called the order a blatant attack on that right.
Rep. Jamie Raskin called it totally unprecedented and blatantly unlawful. He said contractors have a duty and a right to speak truthfully when Congress calls.
The order is seen as shielding top officials, donors and Trump family members from Democratic investigations.
Threatened contract suspension or termination could deter companies from cooperating with lawful requests.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions stated by the White House in its order and fact sheet, and by White House counsel Will Scharf.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Reps. Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia and other congressional Democrats.
evidence_left: Trump signed the order late Friday Nov. 20. It applies to all federal contractors and subcontractors and requires them to notify the White House of congressional requests (ABC News).
It directs contractors to withhold material the White House deems privileged. Firms that do not comply could have contracts suspended or terminated (Philadelphia Inquirer).
evidence_right: Democrats won both chambers in this month's midterms and take control in January (MS NOW, Al Jazeera).
Courts can intervene in disputes over Congress's authority to obtain information, and a dispute over a privilege claim could end up in court (The Hill, Truthout).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from ABC News, NBC News, Philadelphia Inquirer, The Hill, November 23, 2026.

stories.headline: Trump Says US and China Will Pursue 'Joint Guardrails' on AI
stories.dek: Details are thin, while governors press Congress for a national AI framework.
pole_a_bullets: Trump earlier warned that regulation could stifle innovation. Heavy rules risk slowing US AI development.
Any US-China understanding should stay narrow. Bessent said the military-AI point has nothing to do with competition between the two countries.
A patchwork of state laws could burden developers. A single national approach would give companies consistency.
Governors themselves say policy should promote innovation and AI adoption alongside protections.
pole_b_bullets: Xi told Trump the two countries should keep AI under human control. Guardrails need to be real, not slogans.
The announced guardrails lack specifics, so enforcement and scope remain unclear.
States such as California, Colorado, Texas and New York already have AI laws. The governors want federal rules on the most powerful models while states keep consumer, worker and child protections.
Anti-tech backlash helped drive Republican midterm losses, so public pressure for AI rules is rising.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by the Trump administration and industry-friendly AI proponents, as reported by Semafor and SCMP.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Xi (via Xinhua), the National Governors Association and AI-safety advocates.
evidence_left: Trump said Friday Nov. 20 that the US would work with China on 'joint guardrails' for AI (Semafor).
Bessent said Trump and Xi agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions involving AI. The Shenzhen APEC meeting was their third in-person meeting this year (SCMP).
evidence_right: Xinhua reported Xi said the countries should work to ensure AI remains under human control (SCMP). Explainx.ai reported it found no published joint-guardrails agreement; this is not independently confirmed.
On Nov. 22 the NGA released bipartisan principles calling for a national AI approach that clarifies state and federal roles (National Governors Association).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from Semafor, South China Morning Post, National Governors Association, November 23, 2026.

stories.headline: Nvidia Board Rules Out Huang Return as Stock Slides
stories.dek: Interim CEO Colette Kress leads the chipmaker as investigations and a push to reinstate its co-founder continue.
pole_a_bullets: Huang built Nvidia over 33 years. Supporters argue the company's growth depends on his leadership.
A petition with roughly 180,000-plus signatures, including Elon Musk, argues he may have been forced out without due process.
Trump publicly urged the board to rehire him, arguing for an apology and a return to work.
Operations are intact. Kress raised the growth outlook, and the company says customer commitments and its product roadmap continue.
pole_b_bullets: The board unanimously accepted his resignation and cited conduct inconsistent with company standards. Reinstatement could backfire if more findings emerge.
Reuters reported regulators are looking into accounting irregularities, a governance risk for a company at the center of the AI economy.
Huang and the general counsel face closed-door interviews with three House committees over chip-diversion questions.
Nvidia funds major AI customers, including about $30 billion into OpenAI and $10 billion into Anthropic. Leadership uncertainty adds systemic risk.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by Huang, petition signers including Elon Musk, and President Trump.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Nvidia's board, congressional investigators and market commentators cited by NBC News and Briefs.
evidence_left: Nvidia's 8-K dated Nov. 12 says Huang resigned as president, CEO and director, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey Jones named board chair (SEC).
On Nov. 17 Jones said on the earnings call the board 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO' (PBS, SCMP).
evidence_right: Nvidia shares fell about 14% Friday Nov. 20 (Axios, CNBC, NBC News). ABC News Australia reported a 6.9% decline.
Huang and Nvidia's general counsel are due for closed-door interviews with three House committees in early December (SCMP).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from SEC Form 8-K (NVIDIA), PBS NewsHour (AP), CBS News, Axios, November 23, 2026.

stories.headline: House Panel Data Shows 879,868 Nvidia and AMD Chips Approved for China
stories.dek: The disclosure intensifies scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Lutnick as the administration tightens a remote-access loophole.
pole_a_bullets: Nvidia says its limited H200 shipments were legal and authorized, after a licensing process of more than half a year under strict conditions.
Selling chips abroad can create American jobs and cement American AI as the world standard.
Sales were limited in practice. An analyst told CNBC that Beijing did not approve large-scale imports.
Rules should avoid hurting US firms' overseas business, and the Commerce rule is designed to balance that.
pole_b_bullets: Rep. Gregory Meeks said BIS failed to enforce the rules and approved advanced-chip licenses with little scrutiny.
The Pentagon has identified some of the buyers as having ties to the Chinese military.
Bessent said Treasury wanted export controls on Megaspeed, a Singapore firm under scrutiny, but Commerce was in charge.
Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said Lutnick should face hard questions about whether Chinese firms circumvented the rules.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by Nvidia and AMD spokespeople and administration chip-sales proponents, as reported by CNBC, PBS and CNN.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by House Foreign Affairs Democrats, Sen. John Kennedy, Treasury Secretary Bessent and Sen. Maria Cantwell.
evidence_left: The House Foreign Affairs Committee said BIS approved 879,868 chips across 21 license applications as of May 11 (Epoch Times, CNBC). PBS/AP reported more than 850,000.
Nvidia said it has since stopped shipping H200s to China (Epoch Times).
evidence_right: On Nov. 16 Commerce issued an interim rule requiring licenses for advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. BIS said it was written by and at the direction of Treasury and the NSC (Nextgov, CNBC).
Trump said he has 'not lost confidence' in Lutnick (PBS). Lutnick is expected to testify before the Senate Banking Committee (Washington Post).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNBC, PBS NewsHour (AP), Nextgov/FCW, House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats, November 23, 2026.

stories.headline: UN Talks on AI 'Killer Robots' Extended Two Years Without Binding Rules
stories.dek: Geneva negotiators agreed to 'elaborate' a possible accord by 2028 but made no binding commitment.
pole_a_bullets: The mandate keeps a path to an accord open. Countries agreed to elaborate one by 2028.
Most countries support work toward a new treaty, so momentum exists.
UN disarmament chief Izumi Nakamitsu urged work to begin immediately on the strongest possible instrument.
Consensus bodies are slow by design, and any state can block. Even a softened text is progress in that setting.
pole_b_bullets: Beatrice Fihn of Lex International called the result 'pushing the can down the road' for two more years.
Stop Killer Robots called it a watered-down mandate. Activists blamed obstruction mainly by Russia, with the US also seeking a freer hand.
Armed drones that can strike independently have already been deployed in some conflict zones, according to activists.
Future of Life Institute's Anna Hehir said a two-year timeline risks letting technology outpace regulation.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by UN disarmament officials and treaty-supporting states, as reported by AP.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Stop Killer Robots, Lex International and the Future of Life Institute.
evidence_left: The week-long conference ended Saturday Nov. 21 with a softened agreement to extend talks two years (AP via CP24).
The talks are under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, ratified by 128 countries, where decisions are made by consensus (AP via CP24).
evidence_right: UN Secretary-General António Guterres, who leaves office at year-end, had set a 2026 deadline for launching negotiations toward a binding agreement (1News, AP via CP24).

Countries did not commit to binding rules (AP via CP24, 1News). Nakamitsu's description of the outcome as a significant achievement was reported by World Today News citing GPB; not independently confirmed.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from AP via CP24, 1News, KSL (AP), World Today News, November 23, 2026.
